quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by a strong adult.
Will be safe if they stand on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never stand in the vehicle while it is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never stand in the vehicle while it is moving.
questions.explanation: Children who are too small for regular seat belts need special child seats. No one is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Children must always be properly secured in a seat.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. You should:

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Turn on your signal about 100 feet before the intersection.
Turn your front wheels to the left now to prepare for the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your signal about 100 feet before the intersection.
questions.explanation: Always signal about 100 feet before you turn. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This protects you if another car hits you from behind.

questions.question: A vehicle coming toward you at night has its high beams on and you cannot see the road. You should:

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other vehicle with your peripheral vision.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Does not increase crash risk.
Gives you more time to react to danger.
Often causes risky driving decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often causes risky driving decisions.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and causes drivers to make risky decisions.

questions.question: When driving through a work zone, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through the zone quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
Drive at your normal speed through the zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: Slow down when entering and driving through work zones. Follow posted speed limits and watch for workers and hazards.

questions.question: It is safe to stop on railroad tracks for a short time if you are moving with other vehicles.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Never stop, stand, or park on railroad tracks. Only cross railroad tracks if your entire vehicle can fit on the other side.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: Find a gap large enough for you to safely enter the traffic. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there is no safe gap to merge into.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle:

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because oncoming traffic is unlikely.
By driving onto the shoulder of the highway.
If your lane has a dashed yellow line and the passing lane is clear ahead.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on a hill or in a curve because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never pass by driving onto the highway shoulder. Never pass across a solid yellow line.

questions.question: On a road with multiple lanes, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from the side with the dashed line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed only from the side with the dashed line.
questions.explanation: When one line is solid and one is dashed, only the driver next to the dashed line may pass. The driver next to the solid line may not pass.

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means:

options.text: Vehicles in both directions may pass.
Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line on your side means you may pass.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Drive close to the parked vehicles to give more room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your vehicle and parked vehicles. A person may step out of a parked car without looking. A driver may start moving their vehicle without noticing you.

questions.question: When driving on ice or snow, which technique helps drivers avoid crashes?

options.text: Add extra weight to the vehicle for better traction.
Leave the highway as soon as possible.
Turn on four-wheel drive.
Slow down and leave more space between vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and leave more space between vehicles.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on snowy or icy roads. Slowing down and leaving more distance between vehicles are the best ways to avoid crashes on ice or snow.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign means:

options.text: There is a hazard ahead or danger on the road.
There is a school zone nearby.
There is a public recreation area nearby.
There is food or gas ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a hazard ahead or danger on the road.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers about hazards on the road. These signs are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light warns you that the light will turn red soon. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Keep moving and leave the intersection safely.
Speed up so you don't cause an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep moving and leave the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in an intersection when the light turns yellow, move through it as quickly and safely as possible.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You cannot turn left here.
You can turn left only after you stop.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn left here.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. This sign shows that left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:

options.text: Braking too hard multiple times.
Stopping suddenly.
Turning suddenly.
Driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: As you drive faster, your tires have less time to push water away from the road. At high speeds, your tires may lose grip and slide on water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: Should you always drive slower than other traffic?

options.text: No, because driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes, because it is a good defensive driving technique.
Yes, because it is always safer than driving faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive slower when there is heavy traffic or bad weather. However, driving too slowly and blocking normal traffic flow can result in a ticket.

questions.question: When can you drive on the right shoulder of the road?

options.text: Only when a police officer or official tells you to.
When the car in front of you is going too slow.
When the car in front of you is turning.
When the shoulder is paved.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only when a police officer or official tells you to.
questions.explanation: You can only drive on the shoulder of a road if an official directs you to do so. You may pass on the right only when it is legal and safe.

questions.question: If your tires feel like they have lost grip on the road, you should:

options.text: Slow down by shifting to a lower gear.
Slowly release the gas pedal.
Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your tires lose grip, slowly release the gas pedal. Do not use the brakes or try to turn until your tires grip the road again.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield the right-of-way to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.
Cars coming toward you.
Pedestrians already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to cars coming toward you. Always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: When a school bus picks up or drops off children, what must you do?

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction.
Slow down and get ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop before reaching a school bus that is picking up or dropping off children. This applies whether you are traveling in front of the bus, behind it, or in the opposite direction.

questions.question: In rainy weather, when should you be most careful about turning or stopping?

options.text: After it has rained all day.
About 30 minutes after the rain stops.
During the first 30 minutes of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 30 minutes of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when turning and stopping during the first 30 minutes of rain. Oil from cars has not yet washed away, and it mixes with rain to create a slippery surface.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A divided highway is starting.
A steep hill is ahead.
The overpass ahead has low clearance.
Two lanes of traffic going in opposite directions are about to merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The overpass ahead has low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not go under it if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign.

questions.question: When driving on slippery surfaces like snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Keep traction by following other vehicles closely.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills to prevent skidding on slippery surfaces. Also, stay farther back from other vehicles than usual. Avoid sudden stops. If you do not have antilock brakes, pump the brakes gently to slow down or stop.

questions.question: If you see an animal on the road, what should you do?

options.text: No special action is needed.
Honk your horn.
Pass the animal as close as possible.
Be very cautious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Be very cautious when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly to avoid startling or scaring it.
